name: Prambanan
info: Prambanan is a 9th-century Hindu temple compound in southern Java, Indonesia, dedicated to the Trimūrti of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva and built under the Mataram kings; it is the largest Hindu temple site in Indonesia.

facts.made: Likely begun by Rakai Pikatan and inaugurated by his successor King Lokapala of the Mataram kingdom, then expanded by Balitung Maha Sambu and later Mataram kings such as Daksa and Tulodong
facts.form: A Hindu temple compound on a square plan of three walled zones, once with 240 temple structures; the central Shiva temple is 47 metres tall and 34 metres wide, and Brahma and Vishnu temples are 33 metres tall
facts.where: In the Special Region of Yogyakarta, southern Java, Indonesia, about 17 kilometres northeast of Yogyakarta, on the boundary with Central Java; a UNESCO World Heritage Site
facts.known: the tall central Shiva temple; Ramayana and Bhagavata Purana bas-reliefs; 224 ancillary pervara temples in four rows; the Rara Jonggrang legend; anastylosis reconstruction; Ramayana ballet on full moon nights

t: The compound was likely begun by Rakai Pikatan and inaugurated by King Lokapala, and the Shivagrha inscription of 856 describes a Shiva temple compound resembling Prambanan.
It served as the royal temple of the Mataram kingdom, was abandoned around the middle of the 10th century, and fell into ruin after a major earthquake in the 16th century.
Dutch colonial restoration began in the 1930s, the main Shiva temple was completed in 1953 and the central temples by 1993, but only six of the 224 pervara temples have been fully rebuilt.
dyk: According to the Shivagrha inscription, a public water project moved the course of a river near the temple during its construction; the river is identified as the Opak, which now runs along the western side of the compound.
ev: The Shiva temple was inaugurated, according to the Shivagrha inscription issued by King Lokapala
The Javanese court was moved to East Java by Mpu Sindok, and the temples were abandoned around the middle of the 10th century
The temples collapsed in a major earthquake
Cornelis Antonie Lons, a VOC employee, gave the first report on the ruins in his journal
Nicolaus Engelhard commissioned H.C. Cornelius to clear, measure and draw the site, the first effort to study and restore it
The reconstruction of the main Shiva temple was completed and inaugurated by President Sukarno
The main temples of the central zone were complete and inaugurated by President Suharto
The Abhiṣeka ceremony was held for the first time, to cleanse and sanctify the temple as a focus of Hindu worship

sections.origins:
Prambanan was built in the 9th century in the Prambanan Plain of southern Java, where the court and urban centre of the Mataram kingdom lay nearby. The first building was completed in the mid-9th century. It was likely started by Rakai Pikatan and inaugurated by his successor King Lokapala. A short red-paint script reading "pikatan" on a finial of the balustrade of the Shiva temple is taken to confirm that Pikatan began the work.

Some historians who hold to the dual dynasty theory suggest that the temple was meant as the Hindu Sanjaya dynasty's answer to the Buddhist Sailendra dynasty's Borobudur and Sewu temples nearby, and to mark the Sanjaya return to power in Central Java after almost a century of Sailendra domination. Whatever its motive, the building of this large Hindu temple signified a shift of the Mataram court's patronage from Mahayana Buddhism to Shaivite Hinduism. The Shivagrha inscription of 856, issued by Lokapala, describes a Shiva temple compound resembling Prambanan, inaugurated on 12 November 856; the temple's original name was Shiva-grha, the House of Shiva, or Shiva-laya, the Realm of Shiva.
sections.content:
The compound is dedicated to the Trimūrti, the expression of God as Creator (Brahma), Preserver (Vishnu) and Destroyer (Shiva). Its plan is square, with three zones, each walled and pierced by four gates. The outer zone, once about 390 metres per side, has almost wholly vanished, and its original function is unknown. The middle zone, about 225 metres per side, holds four rows of 44, 52, 60 and 68 pervara (ancillary) temples, 224 in all. The inner zone, the holiest, is a raised platform with eight main shrines and eight small ones.

The three main shrines face east: Shiva in the centre, Vishnu to the north and Brahma to the south, with a vahana temple in front of each for the god's mount: the bull Nandi, the kite Garuda and the swan Hamsa. The Shiva temple, 47 metres tall and 34 metres wide, has five chambers; the central one holds a three-metre statue of Shiva Mahadeva, and the others hold Agastya, Ganesha and Durga as slayer of the Bull demon. Narrative reliefs along the balustrades tell the Ramayana, from the Shiva temple into the Brahma temple, and the stories of Krishna from the Bhagavata Purana on the Vishnu temple. The lower outer walls carry niches with a lion flanked by kalpataru trees, called the Prambanan panel.
sections.making:
The temple was expanded extensively by King Lokapala and Balitung Maha Sambu, and later Mataram kings such as Daksa and Tulodong added hundreds of pervara temples around the chief temple. According to the Shivagrha inscription, a public water project changed the course of a river near the temple during construction. The river, identified as the Opak, was cut along a north to south axis beside the outer wall, and its old course was filled in and levelled to make room for the rows of ancillary temples. Experts suggest the shift was meant to protect the compound from lahar from Mount Merapi.

The design follows Hindu architectural tradition based on Vastu Shastra, with a mandala plan, and was meant to mimic Meru, the holy mountain, the abode of the gods and the home of Shiva. The three zones of the plan and of each temple correspond to the realms of Bhurloka, Bhuvarloka and Svarloka. During restoration a well 5.75 metres deep was found under the centre of the Shiva temple, holding a stone casket on a pile of charcoal, earth and burned animal bones; the casket held copper sheets, 20 coins, jewels and 12 gold leaves cut in shapes including a turtle and a Nāga serpent.
sections.reception:
Prambanan was the royal temple of the Kingdom of Mataram, and most of the state's religious ceremonies and sacrifices were conducted there. Scholars estimate that at the height of the kingdom hundreds of brahmins with their disciples lived within the outer wall. Some archaeologists propose that the statue of Shiva in the central chamber was modelled after King Balitung, as a depiction of his deified self after death; some historians likewise believe that showing Shiva as Mahadeva was meant to personify Balitung as Shiva's reincarnation. The meaning of the pervara rows is debated: some believed they were offered by regional rulers and nobles as a sign of submission, some that the rows matched four castes, and others that they were simply meditation places for priests and worship places for devotees.

After the temples ceased to be an important centre of worship, local Javanese people still knew the ruins but not which kings had built them, and they explained the site with the Rara Jonggrang legend. In it Bandung Bondowoso, helped by spirits, built 999 temples in one night to win the princess; she tricked the spirits into fleeing at a false dawn, and he cursed her into stone, becoming the Durga statue in the north chamber, still called Rara Jonggrang.
sections.survival:
After about 80 years of use and expansion, the temples were abandoned near the middle of the 10th century. In the 930s Mpu Sindok moved the Javanese court to East Java. The reason is not clear; the 1006 eruption of Mount Merapi or a power struggle may have caused the shift. The temples collapsed in a major earthquake in the 16th century. Cornelis Antonie Lons made the first report in 1733, and in 1755 the ruins and the Opak River were used to mark the boundary between the Yogyakarta and Surakarta Sultanates. Nicolaus Engelhard had the site cleared and drawn from 1805, and Colin Mackenzie, a surveyor for Thomas Stamford Raffles, came upon the temples by chance in 1811.

The ruins then stayed neglected for decades. Dutch residents carried off sculptures as garden ornaments, villagers took foundation stones for building, and half-hearted excavations in the 1880s facilitated looting, as many sculptures were taken away for collections. The Dutch colonial government began reconstruction in 1918, with proper restoration from 1930 by the anastylosis method, which reuses the original blocks. It was halted by the economic crisis, the Pacific War and the Indonesian National Revolution, and resumed in 1949.
sections.legacy:
Prambanan is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the largest Hindu temple site in Indonesia, and the second largest in Southeast Asia after Angkor Wat. The Shiva temple was completed in 1953 and inaugurated by Sukarno. The Brahma temple was rebuilt in 1978 to 1987 and the Vishnu temple in 1982 to 1991; by 1993 the main central temples were complete. Because much of the original stonework was stolen and reused elsewhere, the government decided to rebuild a shrine only where at least 75% of its masonry survives. Of the 224 pervara temples, six were fully reconstructed by February 2023; the rest are mostly foundations or scattered stones, and rebuilding them all would take at least 200 years at 8 to 12 months each.

Since the 1960s a Ramayana ballet, the Javanese court dance, has been performed on full moon nights on stages west of the Opak River. After the 1990s reconstruction, Balinese and Javanese Hindu communities revived ceremonies there such as Galungan, Tawur Kesanga and Nyepi. A grand Abhiṣeka ceremony in November 2019, the first held there, was meant to cleanse and sanctify the temple and restore its function as a focus of Hindu worship. The 2006 Yogyakarta earthquake damaged the site, which reopened some weeks later.

summary: Prambanan is a Hindu temple compound in southern Java, begun by the Mataram court in the 9th century and dedicated to Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. It was abandoned, collapsed in an earthquake and was rebuilt from the 1930s by anastylosis; it is a World Heritage Site.
notes: Start 856 is the inauguration date of the Shivagrha inscription; the article says the first building was completed in the mid-9th century, so circa is true.

The article says 'about 80 years' of use and abandonment 'near the half of the 10th century' yet the court moved in the 930s; the cause (1006 Merapi eruption or a power struggle) is left as the article's maybe. The 1006 eruption is also said to follow the abandonment in the article's wording; this oddity is left out of the text.
The article gives '140 inner temples along with 30 main ones' in the architecture section, which contradicts the 240/8 figures; left out.
Tourism, visitor numbers, the 2026 festival and Garuda Indonesia were left out as instructed. The 2006 earthquake is mentioned briefly in legacy.
